Professor Shmuel Levit is an outstanding Israeli endocrinologist engaged in developing advanced methods of treating endocrine disease. His specialisation includes innovative approaches to the treatment of diabetes, diseases of the thyroid and parathyroid glands, and of other organs of hormonal regulation.

Having taken his medical degree in Russia, Professor Levit continued his training and practice in Israel, where he completed a fellowship at the Rabin Medical Centre and its Institute of Endocrinology. Today he not only holds a high place in the Israeli medical community but also works successfully with international patients thanks to his command of English and Russian.

Among the main areas of his work are the treatment of diabetes using modern techniques and drugs, and the treatment of disorders of the pituitary, thyroid and parathyroid glands, along with many other endocrine conditions.

Professor Levit is also actively engaged in research, with many publications in respected medical journals and participation in international conferences. His research is aimed at developing and introducing new treatments, particularly for severe forms of diabetes. Levit works closely with the Institute of Endocrinology, where many of his research projects are carried out.

EDUCATION

  • State Medical University in St Petersburg, Russia
  • Fellowship in endocrinology at the Institute of Endocrinology, Beilinson Medical Centre, Israel

LANGUAGES

  • Russian
  • Hebrew
  • English

MEMBERSHIP OF INTERNATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS

  • Israel Medical Association
  • Israel Endocrine Society
  • Israel Diabetes Association
  • European Society of Endocrinology

Avraham Shpirer is an outstanding specialist in ophthalmology, focusing on the treatment of the various structures of the eye — the retina, lens, cornea, vitreous body, tear ducts, eyelids and others. He specialises in paediatric ophthalmology, treating patients of all ages, including newborns and infants. He works actively on retinopathy in premature and low-birth-weight babies, offering distinctive methods such as laser and vitreoretinal surgery.

Key qualities of Avraham Shpirer:

  • A gentle and caring manner with newborns
  • A priority on preserving sight and preventing problems in the future
  • Close collaboration with doctors in other fields, such as paediatricians, neonatologists and neurologists

Education and specialisations:

  • School of Medicine, Tel Aviv University
  • Residency at the Chaim Sheba clinic, specialising in ophthalmology
  • Retraining as a paediatric ophthalmologist and eye surgeon at Mount Sinai Hospital, New York
  • Fellowship in the correction of squint at the university clinic in Los Angeles

Professional achievements:

  • Publications in research journals, including papers, monographs and teaching materials
  • Reviewing and publication of work in respected medical journals
  • Coordinator of clinical trials of new drugs and eye treatment techniques
  • Honorary member of the American association of paediatric ophthalmology and of the Israel Ophthalmological Society
  • Professor of medicine

Areas of work:

  • Paediatric ophthalmology, including infants
  • Diagnosis and treatment of various disorders, such as retinopathy of prematurity, squint, short-sightedness, long-sightedness, astigmatism, raised intraocular pressure, glaucoma, cataract, and chronic viral and bacterial eye disease.

Specialisation: oncologist, radiologist

Main areas of specialisation:

Dr Svetlana Zalmanova is a leading radiation oncologist in Israel and one of the best specialists in brachytherapy (contact radiation therapy) and radiology. She specialises in treating various tumours and cancers using the newest methods of radiation therapy.

  • Tumours of the tongue and oral cavity
  • Tumours of the lip
  • Tumours of the upper and lower jaw
  • Tumours of the urogenital and salivary glands
  • Cancers of the digestive tract
  • Tumours of the urinary and reproductive organs
  • Breast cancer
  • Lung cancer
  • Skin cancer
  • Blood cancer

Summary:

Dr Svetlana Zalmanova is a leading radiation oncologist in Israel with more than 35 years of experience. She heads the radiology department of the Assuta medical centre and is an excellent specialist in her field, applying the most modern methods of treating benign and malignant tumours. Dr Zalmanova is actively engaged in research, developing new ways of applying radiation therapy in malignant disease, including modern methods of brachytherapy with directed delivery to the tumour.

Education and clinical experience:

  • Medical faculty of the First Moscow Medical Institute, Russia
  • Specialisation in radiology at the Cookridge Cancer Hospital radiotherapy centre, England
  • Fellowship in radiotherapy for brain tumours at Brainlab Academy Radiotherapy Training, Germany
  • Fellowship in IMRT/RA and the use of Varian systems at a clinic in Copenhagen, Denmark
  • Advanced training at leading clinics in Europe and the United States

Additional specialisation:

  • Brachytherapy
  • Carcinoma in various locations
  • Benign and malignant brain tumours
  • Retinoblastoma

Academic and research work:

Dr Zalmanova is the author of numerous papers on radiation therapy and brachytherapy and takes an active part in international medical congresses and conferences. Her professional opinion is regarded as authoritative among colleagues from countries around the world.

Membership of international associations:

  • Israel Medical Association (IMA)
  • Israel Society of Clinical Oncology and Radiation Therapy (ISCORT)
  • European Society for Radiotherapy and Oncology (ESTRO)
  • American Society for Radiation Oncology (ASTRO)

Languages:

  • Hebrew
  • English
  • Russian

Dr Svetlana Zalmanova is recognised as one of the most experienced and authoritative specialists in her field; thanks to her innovative treatment methods many patients have received medical care of the highest quality and improved their quality of life.

Dr Tamar Shalev: a leading expert in gastroenterology

Professional overview:
Dr Tamar Shalev, a graduate of the Medical Academy of Latvia in Riga, is a senior physician at the Institute of Gastroenterology of the Wolfson Medical Centre in Israel. She specialises in advanced endoscopy and is recognised for her skill in diagnostic and therapeutic endoscopic ultrasound and in the endoscopic removal of complex polyps.

Main specialisations:

  • Diseases of the digestive tract: diagnosis and treatment of all kinds, including cancer prevention, reflux and peptic ulcer disease.
  • Advanced endoscopy: high expertise in diagnostic and therapeutic endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) and the removal of complex polyps.
  • Inflammatory bowel disease: expert in the treatment of Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.
  • Liver disease: specialist treatment of viral hepatitis, fatty liver disease and autoimmune liver conditions.

Clinical path:

  • Sheba Medical Centre, 2004: completed an internship in internal medicine.
  • Edith Wolfson Medical Centre: completed a fellowship in gastroenterology in 2007.
  • Wolfson Medical Centre: senior physician at the Institute of Gastroenterology and head of the endoscopic ultrasound service since 2019.

Academic and research achievements:

  • Teaching: teacher at the Sackler School of Medicine, Tel Aviv University.
  • Publications: author of research papers in international journals on gastroenterology and internal medicine.
  • Symposia: regular participation in Israeli and international symposia on gastroenterology.

Membership of international associations:

  • Israel Gastroenterology Association
  • European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy
  • American Gastroenterological Association

Dr Shalev continues to make a significant contribution to medicine, giving patients access to the most modern treatments and actively developing the medical community.

Professor Tatiana Gurevich is a leading neurologist and an expert of the highest level in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the nervous system. Her specialisation includes the treatment of Parkinson's disease, epilepsy, movement disorders, Tourette syndrome, headache, spastic pain, chronic pain syndromes, multiple system atrophy and many other neurological conditions. She is also recognised as an authority in neurological rehabilitation.

Over three decades of practice Professor Gurevich has brought relief to thousands of patients, helping them rid themselves of pain and restore their quality of life. Her approach combines rich experience with the use of the newest methods and technologies in neurology.

Her achievements in medicine have repeatedly been recognised with various prizes. In 2001, for example, she received a special award from the Israeli Ministry of Health and a substantial grant from the European Union for her research.

Besides her practice, Professor Gurevich is known as an excellent lecturer and teaches at a number of institutions in Israel. Her expert opinion is also frequently sought by international medical journals on questions of neurology, neuropharmacology and neuropsychiatry.

EDUCATION

  • Faculty of medicine, university in St Petersburg, Russia
  • Residency in neurology at the Ichilov clinic, Tel Aviv, Israel
  • Fellowships in specialist fields at clinics in the United States and Germany

LANGUAGES

  • Russian
  • Hebrew
  • English

MEMBERSHIP OF INTERNATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS

  • Israel Neurological Association (INA)
  • Israel movement disorder society (MDS)

Dr Uri Gur is one of Israel's most highly regarded urologists, with extensive experience in treating conditions of the urinary and reproductive systems in adults and children alike. He is among the leaders of a urology department and also sees patients privately.

This outstanding specialist has exceptional skills and knowledge in reconstructive urology, which allows him to restore the function and integrity of organs of the urinary and reproductive systems that have been damaged or affected by congenital abnormalities.

Among the procedures Dr Gur performs successfully are minimally invasive operations for hydronephrosis, in which he removes the narrowed sections and restores the connection between the ureter and the renal pelvis. His expertise also covers the treatment of urethral strictures arising from injury or congenital abnormality, and he carries out the diagnostic assessment himself before choosing a treatment approach.

Dr Gur also specialises in correcting curvature of the penis, including in Peyronie's disease, and is an expert in the treatment of male infertility and impotence.

In addition to the procedures above, Dr Gur helps men suffering from urinary incontinence after removal of the prostate. He also uses extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy to break up stones in the urinary tract, performs prostate surgery and successfully operates to treat varicocele and hydrocele.

EDUCATION

  • Tel Aviv University — graduated from the faculty of medicine and took a doctoral degree in medical sciences
  • HaSharon hospital (Petah Tikva, Israel) — completed an internship
  • Rabin Medical Centre (Petah Tikva, Israel) — completed a residency in urology
  • Eastern Virginia Medical School (Norfolk, Virginia, USA) — fellowship in reconstructive urology in children and adults

MEMBERSHIP OF MEDICAL ASSOCIATIONS

  • Israel Medical Association
  • Israel Urological Association
  • Member of the European board for the treatment of sexual disorders
  • American Urological Association
  • Israel society for the treatment of sexual disorders
  • European Society for Sexual Medicine
  • European Association of Urology

A leading neurologist in Israel specialising in the treatment of ADHD and in rehabilitation after injury, Dr Veronica Chernuha has earned the respect and trust of colleagues and patients over 25 years of professional work. Her expertise attracts not only local patients but also those who come for treatment from abroad.

Although Dr Chernuha follows the latest developments in medicine worldwide, she also contributes actively to her own field. Her education began at the Omsk Medical Academy in Russia, and after moving to Israel she was successfully certified at Ben-Gurion University.

Her specialisation in paediatric medicine was completed in the paediatrics department of the HaEmek Medical Centre between 2007 and 2011. Later, in 2012, Dr Chernuha took further training in neurology at Tel Aviv University. In 2017 she focused particularly on the treatment of refractory epilepsy in children.

In research, Dr Chernuha takes an active part in international symposia and conferences held in Israel. Her studies are published regularly in respected medical journals. One of her papers, on the effect of innovative drugs on refractory epilepsy in children, published in the journal Epilepsy & Behavior, attracted particular interest in the medical community.

EDUCATION

  • Omsk Medical Academy (Russia)
  • Ben-Gurion University (Israel)
  • Tel Aviv University (Israel)

MEMBERSHIP OF INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS

  • Israel Medical Association (IMA).
  • Israel Society of Clinical Paediatrics.
  • Israel Child Neurology Society.
  • Israel League Against Epilepsy;
  • International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE);
  • European Paediatric Neurology Society (EPNS);
  • International Child Neurology Association (ICNA);
  • Association for child development and rehabilitation, Israel.
